questions: If there are multiple ways to choose K elements that include A_i and yield different GCDs, should we output the maximum, minimum, or something else?
When K = 1, is the answer simply A_i for each i, or is there any special handling?
Are the K chosen elements required to be distinct positions in the sequence, or can the same value at different indices be considered separate?
Must the K elements be chosen in the original order (i.e., a subsequence), or can they be any K elements regardless of their positions?
If N = K, does the answer for each i equal the GCD of the entire array, or is there any other rule?
Are there any constraints on the time limit or memory usage that affect the choice of algorithm?
Should the output GCD values be printed as integers on separate lines without any extra spaces or formatting?
In case the GCD computation involves large numbers, is there any modulo requirement for the output?
answers: For each i, the task is to find the maximum possible GCD among all selections of K elements that include A_i.
Yes, when K=1 the only choice is A_i itself, so the answer is A_i.
Positions are treated as distinct even if values repeat, so equal values at different indices count as separate elements.
The order of the chosen K elements does not matter since GCD is order-independent.
Yes, when N=K the only choice is the whole array, so the answer is its GCD.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume standard algorithmic time/memory limits for this constraint size.
Each answer should be printed on its own line, as already stated in the Output section.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume standard integer output with no modulo requirement.
inline_prompts: You are given a sequence A = (A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N) of length N and a positive integer K. For each i = 1, 2, \dots, N, solve the following problem: When you choose K elements from A that include A_i, find the maximum possible GCD (greatest common divisor) of those chosen elements. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N K A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print N lines. The j-th line should contain the answer for i=j. Constraints - 1 \leq K \leq N \leq 1.2 \times 10^6 - 1 \leq A_i \leq 10^6 - All input values are integers.
